Subject: Post-demo: curated engine shortlist, economics & prompt pack (next steps)

Hi Carlos / Amira — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the three recommended inference paths tailored to the Clearline use case (customer-facing summarization + structured extraction at ~1.5k tokens average):

Summary recommendation (shortlist):
- Redwood-RT-2.1 (quantized): best latency and predictable p99 at target throughput. Strong at structured extraction and stable on long prompts.
- OpenTrident-13B-INT8: cost-efficient middle ground; good throughput with modest latency but slightly lower extraction precision in some prompt slices.
- LlamaMax-70B-8Q (server-optimized): highest quality on nuanced summaries, higher cost and higher p99 — recommended only for latency-tolerant paths or small sampling.

Economic & latency estimates (ballpark, per 1M input+output tokens):
- Redwood-RT-2.1 (quantized): ~$220 / 1M tokens; p50 ~45ms, p95 ~110ms, p99 ~160ms on Dedicated T4 pool.
- OpenTrident-13B-INT8: ~$90 / 1M tokens; p50 ~60ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~320ms.
- LlamaMax-70B-8Q: ~$950 / 1M tokens; p50 ~120ms, p95 ~320ms, p99 ~560ms.

Key tradeoffs to note:
- Quality vs cost: LlamaMax gives best human evals for abstractive summaries; Redwood-RT is near-par for structured extractions but much lower unit cost.
- Latency SLO: if you need p95 <150ms for synchronous UI flows, Redwood-RT is the only one that meets that consistently at your anticipated concurrency.
- Regression risk: we saw two prompt slices during the demo where OpenTrident produced hallucinated fields for long, nested bullet inputs — we include an eval checklist and regression guardrail in the prompt pack.

Deliverables attached / links below:
- clearline-prompt-pack-v1.zip (sample prompt templates, canonical extraction labels, regression test harness)
- benchmarks-clearline-20280630.csv (end-to-end latency/cost samples from the demo run)
- redwood-quote-v2.pdf (updated cost spreadsheet + optional reserved capacity tiers)

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) You confirm which engine(s) to pilot (by 2028-07-03).
2) We provision a 2-week evaluation sandbox (dedicated routing + prefix caching) and load sample prompt set — Redwood sets up. (Target start: 2028-07-06)
3) Karthik runs targeted regression tests and sends detailed failure cases; Monica will propose an enablement plan for integration (by 2028-07-09).
4) Procurement review of quote; Vanessa to follow up with updated DocuSign link and a short-term pilot contract (by 2028-07-05).

Ping if you'd like a 30-min working session with Karthik to walk the prompt pack and benchmark CSV line-by-line.

Hi Carlos — quick answers inline and a few concrete mitigations we used in the demo: 

1) Hosted vs Dedicated pricing delta: for the pilot volumes you described (~3-5M tokens / month), hosted incremental unit is ~20-35% higher than the reserved Dedicated tier. The attached redwood-quote-v2.pdf has two example purchase bands (monthly reserved and on-demand). If you expect steady traffic, reserved gives immediate payback.

2) OpenTrident regression mitigations (no model swap required):
- Prompt canonicalization: normalize nested bullets to single-line markers (prompt pack example: /normalize-bullets).
- Two-pass validation: run a lightweight extractor on the first pass and apply a stricter regex-based QA filter; if it fails confidence threshold, route to LlamaMax or flag for human review.
- Safety soft-filter: apply a small curated hallucination-detector model (cheap, <10ms inference) before commit.

3) Audit logs / SOC 2: Monica is attaching the SOC 2 summary (redacted) and our log retention policy; for pilot we can set log retention to 30 days and provide field-level redaction for PII in logs. For production, we can enable customer-managed KMS and extended retention per contract.

Feasibility of model-level routing: yes — Redwood routing supports policy-based routing (latency-first primary + quality fallback). We can configure probabilistic canary or deterministic fallback on low-confidence outputs. We'll include a sample routing policy in the sandbox.

Benchmarks link and instructions: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cClearlineBenchmarks — bench CSV includes raw token counts, GPU type, and p95/p99 lines. Look at rows tagged "demo-20280630" for the exact runs we used.

I will also prepare a small test harness (open-source) that you can run locally to reproduce the regression case you saw; Karthik will share the repo link within 24h.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
